newsitem.title: FRANCE: Film star Tapie draws a veil on political career.
newsitem.headline: Film star Tapie draws a veil on political career.

text.p: Former businessman and soccer boss Bernard Tapie, set on a film career after controversial star-billing in a new movie, has given formal notice relinquishing his seat in the National Assembly, the chamber said on Tuesday.
The flamboyant Tapie, 53, in a publicity stunt timed to match the launch of "Men, Women: Instructions for Use", announced last week that he would resign by last Wednesday.
But it was only this week that Philippe Seguin, speaker of the lower house, received Tapie's written request.

Seguin's office said in a statement Tapie had notified his resignation as deputy of the Bouches du Rhone department in southern France. Seguin replied that it would take effect on Wednesday when it is published in the Official Journal.

Tapie, target of a blizzard of legal suits over his now-destroyed business empire and the Marseille soccer team he once ran, sparked more controversy with his role as a power-hungry and morally dubious lawyer in Claude Lelouche's film.

Critics said Tapie gave a convincing performance, and the film's opening pulled in the crowds. But a host of newspaper commentators accused Lelouche of sacrificing morals for money in hiring a man with three criminal convictions.
"I have paid too dearly for mixing two careers," Tapie said last week. "In France, you cannot be a film artist and a national politician at the same time."
Tapie, a member of the small Radical party, was first elected in 1989 and was re-elected in 1993.
Justice Minister Jacques Toubon last month began the formal process of ejecting Tapie from the French parliament as well as stripping him of his seat in the European parliament.
The French procedure is due to be completed by October 2, when the Assembly is to reconvene after a summer break, but the European procedure is expected to take longer.

Tapie faces a probable spell in prison after he lost his parliamentary immunity, since two appeal courts have confirmed jail sentences of eight and six months against him for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match. He is appealing in both cases to the Supreme Court.
